title: Clamp an infusion pump to its IV pole at the tape: hold it up level while the other hand screws the pole clamp tight
instruction: Mount the pump on the pole at the tape.
context: Nurses mount infusion pumps on IV poles to set up pump-run infusions: RNs (O*NET 29-1141.00, 3.47 M jobs: 'Administer medications to patients') and LPNs (29-2061.00, 0.67 M: 'start intravenous fluids'). BD's Alaris GP directions: 'Place pump around pole and tighten screw until the clamp is secured to the pole' and 'Never mount the pump such that the infusion stand becomes top heavy'. The pump hangs off the pole's axis, so one hand holds it level at the mark until the jaw bites while the other turns the knob; let go early and it drops, and a dropped pump must be taken out of service.
setup: Positions (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm; heights above the table top. Fixed: an IV pole mast, a stainless steel tube 25 mm across, its axis at (40, 0), standing 55 cm tall in a 60 mm round flange 8 mm thick screwed to the table; a band of yellow tape 50 mm wide round it from 17.5 to 22.5 cm up. Loose: a BD Alaris GP volumetric infusion pump at its real size, 14.8 cm wide x 22.5 cm tall x 14.8 cm deep, grey ABS case on four rubber feet, modelled at 1.0 kg (the real one is about 2.5 kg), standing with its underside's centre at (24.75, 0), face (screen and keys) towards the arms, back towards the pole. Carry handle on top: a 2.0 x 1.6 cm bar 11 cm long running fore and aft, 3.7 cm above the case. Pole clamp folded out on its back: aluminium, a back plate 6 mm proud of the case, a fixed jaw on the pump's left and a moving jaw on its right, both 40 mm tall, centre line 15 cm up; the throat is open to 31 mm (3 mm each side of the pole) and its mouth is 3.1 cm short of the pole. The moving jaw is driven by a right-hand lead screw, 1.75 mm a turn, turned by a black ribbed knob 35 mm across and 25 mm long on the pump's right side, its axis level 15 cm up; about 3.4 turns close the throat onto the pole. Distractors (SimReady, loose, ignored by scoring): a box of examination gloves (cardboard, 17.8 x 11.7 x 5.6 cm, 300 g) at (60, 30) turned 17 degrees; a blue plastic cup (6.4 cm across, 10 cm tall, 20 g) at (60, -30); a box of bandages (cardboard, 4.9 x 5.2 x 4.2 cm, 20 g) at (14, 27).
scoring: Read on video, with a ruler on the pole and a digital angle gauge on the pump's top. 0 if at any moment the pump was dropped (moving down faster than 0.3 m/s, 5 mm or more between two 60 fps frames: dropped or slid down the pole), tipped more than 45 degrees, or fell off the table. Hanging: both clamp jaws within 1 mm of the pole (a 1 mm feeler gauge does not enter either side), the pump's lowest point at least 1 cm above the table, no loose object standing under the pump's outline, and every fingertip at least 3 cm from the pump (case, handle, clamp and knob). The score is read once the pump has been hanging for 3 s without a break: 1.0 if the clamp's centre line is on the tape band (17.5 to 22.5 cm up), the pump is within 3 degrees of upright and it has sunk at most 5 mm since it began hanging; 0.75 on the band and upright but sunk more than 5 mm; 0.5 on the band but more than 3 degrees from upright; 0.25 hanging but the clamp's centre line off the band. 0 otherwise (standing on the table, held, propped, loose on the pole, or not hanging for 3 s).
reset_notes: Lift the pump off the pole after unscrewing the knob about 4 turns, until the throat is 31 mm across (a 31 mm gauge block slides in); stand it on its feet at its tape marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Pump case, handle and clamp are rigid primitives at the Alaris GP's published 148 x 225 x 148 mm (SimReady has no such pump). Mass cut from about 2.5 kg to 1.0 kg so the YAM arms can lift and steady it. The lead screw is code: the moving jaw's drive follows the knob's turns (1.75 mm/turn, estimated), presses the pole with 200 N, then the knob meets a stop. The pole is a fixed tube on the table standing in for an IV stand's mast. Friction 1.0 static, 0.9 dynamic. Distractors are SimReady props.
